question.text: Under SEBI regulations, what is the minimum number of investors required in a mutual fund scheme after the initial NFO period to avoid winding up?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations and related SEBI circulars, every open-ended mutual fund scheme is required to maintain a minimum of 20 investors on a continuous basis after the close of the NFO. A linked condition restricts any single investor from holding more than 25% of the scheme's corpus. If either threshold is breached and not rectified within the prescribed cure period, the scheme must be wound up. The intent is to preserve the "mutual" character of a mutual fund and prevent it from being used as a private investment vehicle. The Trap: 50 and 100 are higher round numbers that sound regulator-like but are not the prescribed minimum. 10 is too low and would defeat the purpose of preserving collective ownership. Note: The cited pages of the NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook (p.79, p.97, p.299, p.303) reference governance / SID provisions on minimum investors but do not explicitly state the 20-investor minimum, the post-NFO maintenance requirement, the 25% single-investor cap, or the winding-up trigger. The framing above is general SEBI mutual fund regulatory knowledge (the so-called "20-25 rule").
